title: In-product copilot
tagline: Help inside the product, scoped to one tenant, metered to the cent.
summary: A SaaS product embeds an assistant that answers from the tenant's own data and proposes typed, reversible actions the user confirms. Every call carries the tenant ID through retrieval, the model gateway and the usage meter, so isolation and billing are provable.
customer_job: Get a task done in the product without leaving the screen or reading the docs.
baseline: Users open support tickets or abandon the feature; the product team cannot price AI features because usage is not attributed.
accepted_result: A suggestion the user applies, inside their tenant, with cost attributed to that tenant.

primary_metric.name: Applied suggestions per active tenant
primary_metric.definition: Suggestions applied without undo within 24 hours, per active tenant per week.

economics.basis: Illustrative assumption measured as user time saved; revenue from pricing the feature is a separate ledger.

components.label: Tenant user
components.detail: Works in the product; opens the copilot in context.

components.label: Product UI with copilot panel
components.detail: Streams answers; shows proposed actions with a diff.

components.label: Edge protection
components.detail: Per-tenant rate limits and abuse controls.

components.label: Tenant identity
components.detail: Session with tenant ID and role claims.

components.label: Copilot API
components.detail: Resolves tenant scope; refuses calls without it.
components.failure_mode: Tenant ID taken from the request body instead of the session.

components.label: Model gateway
components.detail: Per-tenant budget, cache key includes tenant ID.
components.failure_mode: Shared cache returns another tenant's answer.

components.label: Assistant model
components.detail: Fast model for answers; larger model for complex actions.

components.label: Tenant-partitioned index
components.detail: Namespace per tenant; no cross-tenant query path.

components.label: Product actions
components.detail: Typed, reversible operations; writes need user confirmation.

components.label: Usage meter
components.detail: Tokens and actions per tenant, exported to billing.

components.label: Release evals
components.detail: Task set per feature plus cross-tenant probes.

journey.title: Ask in context
journey.narration: The user asks from the screen they are on. The panel sends the question with the current view, never with a tenant ID the client chose.

journey.title: Resolve the tenant
journey.narration: The API takes the tenant from the session. Retrieval can only address that tenant's namespace.

journey.title: Answer with a metered call
journey.narration: The gateway applies the tenant's budget and a cache key that includes the tenant, then meters tokens to that tenant.

journey.title: Propose, confirm, apply
journey.narration: Actions arrive as a dry-run diff. The user confirms; the write returns an undo token.

journey.title: Probe isolation every release
journey.narration: Release evals include requests that try to reach another tenant's data. One success blocks the release.

team.step: Ask, review the diff, confirm or undo
Answer from tenant data; propose typed actions

Finance prices the feature from metered cost

evals.name: Cross-tenant leakage
evals.method: Seeded canary records per tenant; adversarial prompts.

evals.name: Write confirmation
evals.threshold: 100 percent of writes preceded by confirmation

evals.name: Applied suggestion rate
evals.threshold: Tracked per feature; release blocks on a 20 percent drop

risks.risk: Data from one tenant appears for another.
risks.control: Tenant from session only; namespaced index; tenant in cache key; canary probes.

risks.risk: One tenant consumes the AI budget.
risks.control: Per-tenant budget at the gateway and plan-based limits.
Dry-run diff and confirmation enforced in the action layer.

gcp.headline: Cloud Run API with Gemini and AlloyDB row-level security
gcp.notes: Keep vectors beside tenant rows in AlloyDB so row-level security applies to retrieval; meter through BigQuery exports.
gcp.rationale: Database-enforced isolation; Postgres compatibility keeps exit cost moderate.

vercel.headline: Next.js panel, AI Gateway per-tenant budgets, Neon row-level security
vercel.notes: AI SDK streaming in the product UI; gateway tags carry the tenant for usage attribution; Neon branches support preview testing with fixture tenants.
vercel.rationale: The most direct fit for a Next.js SaaS; isolation proof is on the application team.

cloudflare.headline: Workers API, per-tenant Durable Objects and AI Gateway metering
cloudflare.notes: A Durable Object per tenant gives a natural isolation and rate-limit boundary; Vectorize namespaces separate tenant vectors.
cloudflare.rationale: Isolation by construction at low cost; data residency per tenant needs design.

aws.headline: Lambda API, Bedrock with application inference profiles per tier
aws.notes: Inference profiles attribute model cost; Aurora row-level security covers data and vectors.

azure.headline: Container Apps API, Foundry Models, Azure AI Search per-tenant indexes
azure.notes: Index-per-tenant or filter-per-tenant in Azure AI Search depends on tenant count and size.
azure.rationale: Good governance; search units make many small tenants expensive.

railway.headline: API service, Postgres row-level security, direct model API
railway.notes: Workable for an early SaaS; metering and budgets are application code.
railway.rationale: Simple and portable; governance is entirely self-built.
